newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Oil prices could average around $16-$18/bbl-BP.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices could average around $16-$18/bbl-BP.

text.p: World oil prices could average between $16-$18 a barrel over the next few years and refining margins are also expected to stay weak, British Petroleum Plc's Chief Executive John Browne said on Saturday.
Oil prices could stay within "a range that we think of about $16-$18 a barrel," he told Reuters in an interview in Kuwait.
"We might look back and see the prices of last year somewhat out of line with the averages that we are seeing (now)."

Browne, who said he believed it was "foolish" to forecast oil prices, refused to give an exact time period for his projection but said "something like that" when asked if his estimate would be the average for the next three years.
World oil prices fell to six-month lows on Friday to just under $20 -- dropping by 20 percent over the last six weeks.
Browne, who sees world demand growing by two percent a year or two million barrels a day, said the current price "weakness is still quite high" compared to the average price over the past decade.

"There is clearly good underlying demand. Demand seems to be growing well. Last year it was growing very strongly and it started the year off well. But of course there is a lot of supply...," he said.
Browne said that 1997 refining margins were expected to stay low also due to oversupply.

"Refining margins have been very weak and again we see quite a lot of excess capacity coming on the market this year...We believe that the refining margin will remain reletively weak this year," he said, forecasting a margin of "just over" $2 based on BP's benchmark.
Earlier this month, Browne told Reuters that BP's refining margins could improve by around 50 cents if all BP refineries were brought to the same level of efficiency.

Browne, whose visit to Kuwait coincides with an official visit by Britain's Prince Charles, held talks during his two-day stay with senior Kuwaiti oil industry officials. Kuwait has a 9.5 percent stake in BP.
Kuwait's BP equity growth and dividend was valued at $1.8 billion in 1996, executives said.
BP, which last May renewed a 1992 technical assistance accord with the state-owned Kuwait Oil Company, treats the Gulf Arab state "like any other shareholder", Browne said.

Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) member Kuwait has a daily crude output of about two million barrels and plans to raise production capacity to three million barrels early in the next century.
